newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline shunted down by aggressive seller.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline shunted down by aggressive seller.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were shunted sharply lower on Friday afternoon with one U.S. trade house seen selling aggressively, traders said.
A trader at the U.S. trade house blamed poor demand in Europe and the increasing likelihood of being unable to take barges inland because of ice blocked waterways.
"Anyone who is long in ARA at the moment would be advised to sell," the trader said.
However, other traders said the trader was just selling barges off to cover a short against January paper.
"There are one or two big paper longs out there but they don't play the barge market as well as this guy," a trader at a UK major said.

He blamed the lack of demand in Europe, the scarcity of vessels to take product to the U.S. and gasoline's recent strength in relation to naphtha, that has caused both refiners and blenders to maximise output, for growing European avail's and the current volatility.

The trader at the U.S. trade house said the arbitrage to the U.S. was workable but expensive freight meant that this was now more dependent on quality with recent price falls in the U.S. cutting options to move Eurograde.
Eurograde barges traded at $219 down to $217 a tonne fob ARA slipping from around $224 in early business.
The weaker spot market saw January swaps trading $2 lower at $218.75 a tonne fob ARA.
Underlying interest to move product transatlantic and tight freight space pegged cargo prices stable with the discount to ARA barges narrowing to around $8 from $10 a tonne.
